jerusalem_636.name: Jerusalem
jerusalem_636.what: The city David made Israel's capital, site of God's temple and of Jesus' death and resurrection.
key: David captured the Jebusite stronghold and made Jerusalem his royal city (2 Samuel 5).
Solomon dedicated the temple, and the glory of the LORD filled it (1 Kings 8).
The Babylonians burned the temple and the city and carried the people into exile (2 Kings 25).
Jesus was crucified just outside the city and laid in a nearby tomb (Luke 23).
The Holy Spirit came upon the disciples at Pentecost, and about three thousand believed (Acts 2).

egypt_362.name: Egypt
egypt_362.what: The great kingdom of the Nile valley, where Israel grew into a nation and was later enslaved.
key: Abram went down to Egypt during a famine in Canaan (Genesis 12).
Joseph, sold by his brothers, rose to rule over all Egypt under Pharaoh (Genesis 41).
Jacob and his whole family moved to Egypt and settled in Goshen (Genesis 46).
After the tenth plague, the LORD brought Israel out of Egypt on Passover night (Exodus 12).
Joseph took Mary and the child Jesus to Egypt to escape Herod (Matthew 2).

babylon_151.name: Babylon
babylon_151.what: The capital of the Babylonian Empire on the Euphrates, where Judah was taken into exile.
key: Hezekiah showed all his treasures to envoys from Babylon (2 Kings 20).
Nebuchadnezzar took Jerusalem and carried its king and people to Babylon (2 Kings 24).
Jeremiah wrote to the exiles, telling them to seek the welfare of Babylon (Jeremiah 29).
Daniel read the writing on the wall the night Babylon fell (Daniel 5).
John saw the fall of Babylon the great, the city opposed to God (Revelation 18).

jordan_653.name: Jordan
jordan_653.what: The river flowing from the Sea of Galilee to the Dead Sea, the eastern boundary of Canaan.
jordan_653.today: Jordan River, between Israel, the West Bank, and Jordan
key: Jacob crossed the Jordan with only his staff on his way to Haran (Genesis 32).
The waters stopped when the priests' feet touched them, and Israel crossed on dry ground (Joshua 3).
Elijah struck the water with his cloak, and he and Elisha crossed over (2 Kings 2).
Naaman washed seven times in the Jordan and was healed of leprosy (2 Kings 5).
Jesus was baptized by John in the Jordan (Matthew 3).

moab_815.name: Moab
moab_815.what: A kingdom east of the Dead Sea, descended from Lot and often hostile to Israel.
moab_815.today: West-central Jordan, east of the Dead Sea
key: Balak king of Moab hired Balaam to curse Israel, but he blessed them instead (Numbers 22).
Moses died in the land of Moab after viewing the promised land (Deuteronomy 34).
Ehud killed Eglon king of Moab and freed Israel (Judges 3).
Ruth the Moabite returned with Naomi to Bethlehem (Ruth 1).
Mesha king of Moab rebelled against Israel after Ahab died (2 Kings 3).

zion_1263.name: Zion
zion_1263.what: The hill in Jerusalem David captured; the name extends to the temple mount, the city, and God's people.
key: David captured the stronghold of Zion and called it the city of David (2 Samuel 5).
Solomon brought the ark up from Zion into the new temple (1 Kings 8).
God declares that he has set his King on Zion, his holy hill (Psalms 2).
Isaiah foresaw the law going out from Zion to the nations (Isaiah 2).
Peter applies Isaiah's cornerstone laid in Zion to Christ (1 Peter 2).

assyria_111.name: Assyria
assyria_111.what: A powerful Mesopotamian empire on the upper Tigris that conquered the northern kingdom of Israel.
key: The Tigris is described as flowing east of Assyria (Genesis 2).
The king of Assyria captured Samaria and deported Israel because of their sin (2 Kings 17).
Sennacherib invaded Judah, but the angel of the LORD struck his army (2 Kings 19).
God calls Assyria the rod of his anger against a godless nation (Isaiah 10).
Nahum announced the downfall of Assyria's capital, Nineveh (Nahum 3).

samaria_1022.name: Samaria
samaria_1022.what: The capital of the northern kingdom of Israel, and later the hill region between Galilee and Judea.
samaria_1022.today: Sebastia, near Nablus, West Bank (the city); central hill country (the region)
key: King Omri bought the hill of Samaria and built his capital there (1 Kings 16).
During a severe siege, four lepers found the Syrian camp deserted (2 Kings 7).
Samaria fell to Assyria, and Israel was carried into exile (2 Kings 17).
Jesus spoke with a Samaritan woman at Jacob's well (John 4).
Philip preached Christ in Samaria, and many believed and were baptized (Acts 8).

gilead_475.name: Gilead
gilead_475.what: A fertile, hilly region east of the Jordan River, settled by Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh.
gilead_475.today: Northwestern Jordan, east of the Jordan River
key: Jacob and Laban made a covenant in the hill country of Gilead (Genesis 31).
Reuben and Gad asked for Gilead because it suited their livestock (Numbers 32).
Jephthah the Gileadite led Israel against the Ammonites (Judges 11).
Elijah the Tishbite, from Gilead, announced a drought to Ahab (1 Kings 17).
Jeremiah lamented, asking whether there was no balm in Gilead (Jeremiah 8).

edom_357.name: Edom
edom_357.what: The land of Esau's descendants, south and southeast of the Dead Sea.
key: Esau, also called Edom, settled in the hill country of Seir (Genesis 36).
The king of Edom refused to let Israel pass through his land (Numbers 20).
David put garrisons throughout Edom, and the Edomites became his servants (2 Samuel 8).
Edom revolted from Judah and set up its own king (2 Kings 8).
Obadiah announced judgment on Edom for its violence against Jacob (Obadiah 1).

canaan_272.name: Canaan
canaan_272.what: The land between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean that God promised to Abraham's offspring.
canaan_272.today: Roughly modern Israel, the Palestinian territories, and Lebanon
key: Abram arrived in Canaan, and the LORD promised the land to his offspring (Genesis 12).
God promised all the land of Canaan as an everlasting possession (Genesis 17).
During a famine, Jacob sent his sons from Canaan to buy grain in Egypt (Genesis 42).
Moses sent twelve spies to explore the land of Canaan (Numbers 13).
Joshua and Eleazar distributed Canaan to the tribes of Israel (Joshua 14).

syria_1122.name: Syria
syria_1122.what: The Aramean kingdom north of Israel centered on Damascus; later a Roman province including Antioch.
key: Ahab was killed in battle against the Syrians at Ramoth-gilead (1 Kings 22).
Naaman, commander of Syria's army, came to Elisha to be healed (2 Kings 5).
Syria and Israel joined against Ahaz, and Isaiah gave the Immanuel sign (Isaiah 7).
Quirinius was governor of Syria at the time of Jesus' birth (Luke 2).
After his conversion, Paul went into the regions of Syria and Cilicia (Galatians 1).

galilee_433.name: Galilee
galilee_433.what: The northern region of Israel around the Sea of Galilee, where Jesus grew up and did most of his ministry.
key: Kedesh in Galilee was set apart as a city of refuge (Joshua 20).
Isaiah foretold a great light for Galilee of the nations (Isaiah 9).
Jesus began preaching and calling disciples in Galilee (Matthew 4).
At a wedding in Cana in Galilee, Jesus turned water into wine (John 2).
The risen Jesus met the eleven on a mountain in Galilee and sent them out (Matthew 28).

bethel_202.name: Bethel
bethel_202.what: A town north of Jerusalem where God met Jacob, later a center of idolatrous worship in Israel.
bethel_202.today: Likely Beitin, north of Jerusalem, West Bank
key: Abram built an altar between Bethel and Ai (Genesis 12).
Jacob dreamed of a ladder to heaven and named the place Bethel (Genesis 28).
Jeroboam set up a golden calf at Bethel for the northern tribes (1 Kings 12).
Josiah tore down the altar at Bethel, fulfilling an earlier prophecy (2 Kings 23).
Amaziah the priest of Bethel ordered Amos to leave (Amos 7).

jericho_634.name: Jericho
jericho_634.what: An ancient oasis city near the Jordan River, the first city Israel conquered in Canaan.
jericho_634.today: Tell es-Sultan, near Jericho, West Bank
key: Rahab hid the two Israelite spies in Jericho (Joshua 2).
The walls fell after Israel marched around the city for seven days (Joshua 6).
Hiel rebuilt Jericho at the cost of his sons, as Joshua had warned (1 Kings 16).
Elisha healed Jericho's bad spring with a bowl of salt (2 Kings 2).
Jesus called Zacchaeus down from a tree in Jericho (Luke 19).

hebron_551.name: Hebron
hebron_551.what: An ancient city in the hill country of Judah, linked with Abraham and David's early reign.
key: Abraham buried Sarah in the cave of Machpelah near Hebron (Genesis 23).
Caleb received Hebron as his inheritance (Joshua 14).
David was anointed king over Judah at Hebron (2 Samuel 2).
All the tribes came to Hebron and anointed David king over Israel (2 Samuel 5).
Absalom began his rebellion against David at Hebron (2 Samuel 15).

lebanon_720.name: Lebanon
lebanon_720.what: The mountain range north of Israel, famous for its cedar forests.
key: God promised Israel territory from the wilderness to Lebanon (Joshua 1).
Hiram of Tyre supplied cedars of Lebanon for Solomon's temple (1 Kings 5).
Cedars from Lebanon were brought for rebuilding the temple after the exile (Ezra 3).
The righteous are said to grow like a cedar in Lebanon (Psalms 92).

damascus_322.name: Damascus
damascus_322.what: An ancient city northeast of Israel, the capital of Syria (Aram).
key: Abram pursued the captors of Lot as far as north of Damascus (Genesis 14).
Naaman boasted that the rivers of Damascus were better than the Jordan (2 Kings 5).
King Ahaz copied an altar he saw in Damascus for the temple (2 Kings 16).
Saul met the risen Jesus on the road to Damascus (Acts 9).
Paul escaped Damascus by being lowered over the wall in a basket (2 Corinthians 11).

bashan_159.name: Bashan
bashan_159.what: A fertile highland east of the Sea of Galilee, known for its cattle and oaks.
key: Israel defeated Og king of Bashan at Edrei (Numbers 21).
Moses gave Bashan to the half-tribe of Manasseh (Deuteronomy 3).
The psalmist describes his enemies as strong bulls of Bashan (Psalms 22).
Amos rebuked the women of Samaria as cows of Bashan (Amos 4).

tyre_1184.name: Tyre
tyre_1184.what: A wealthy Phoenician port city on the Mediterranean coast north of Israel.
key: Hiram king of Tyre sent cedar and craftsmen to build David's house (2 Samuel 5).
Hiram supplied timber for Solomon's temple in exchange for food (1 Kings 5).
Ezekiel prophesied that Tyre would become a bare rock for drying nets (Ezekiel 26).
Jesus healed the daughter of a Gentile woman in the region of Tyre (Mark 7).
Paul stayed seven days with disciples at Tyre (Acts 21).

sodom_1107.name: Sodom
sodom_1107.what: A city in the Jordan valley destroyed by God for its great wickedness.
sodom_1107.today: Exact site unknown; probably near the Dead Sea
key: Lot chose the Jordan valley and moved his tent as far as Sodom (Genesis 13).
Abraham pleaded with the LORD to spare Sodom for the sake of the righteous (Genesis 18).
The LORD rained sulfur and fire on Sodom after rescuing Lot (Genesis 19).
Jesus said judgment would be more bearable for Sodom than for unrepentant towns (Matthew 11).
Peter cites Sodom's destruction as an example of God's judgment (2 Peter 2).

judea_657.name: Judea
judea_657.what: The southern region around Jerusalem, the former territory of Judah, a Roman district in New Testament times.
judea_657.today: Southern Israel and the West Bank around Jerusalem
key: Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea (Matthew 2).
John the Baptist preached in the wilderness of Judea (Matthew 3).
Jesus returned to Judea to raise Lazarus (John 11).
Jesus sent his disciples to be witnesses in Judea, Samaria, and beyond (Acts 1).
Men from Judea taught that Gentiles must be circumcised, prompting the Jerusalem council (Acts 15).

midian_796.name: Midian
midian_796.what: The desert homeland of the Midianites, east of the Gulf of Aqaba.
key: Moses fled from Pharaoh to the land of Midian (Exodus 2).
Moses tended the flock of Jethro, the priest of Midian (Exodus 3).
Phinehas killed an Israelite man and a Midianite woman, stopping the plague (Numbers 25).
Gideon and three hundred men routed the Midianite army (Judges 7).

gibeah_466.name: Gibeah
gibeah_466.what: A town of Benjamin north of Jerusalem, King Saul's hometown and capital.
gibeah_466.today: Likely Tell el-Ful, on Jerusalem's northern edge
key: Men of Gibeah abused and killed a Levite's concubine (Judges 19).
Israel's tribes went to war against Gibeah and Benjamin (Judges 20).
Saul returned home to Gibeah after being chosen king (1 Samuel 10).
Seven of Saul's descendants were put to death at Gibeah of Saul (2 Samuel 21).

shechem_1069.name: Shechem
shechem_1069.what: An ancient city in the hill country of Ephraim, between Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim.
key: Abram built his first altar in Canaan at Shechem (Genesis 12).
Simeon and Levi killed the men of Shechem after Dinah was violated (Genesis 34).
Joshua renewed Israel's covenant at Shechem and Joseph's bones were buried there (Joshua 24).
Abimelech made himself king at Shechem and later destroyed the city (Judges 9).
Israel rejected Rehoboam at Shechem, and the kingdom divided (1 Kings 12).

heshbon_565.name: Heshbon
heshbon_565.what: A city east of the Jordan, the capital of Sihon king of the Amorites.
key: Israel defeated Sihon and took Heshbon, his royal city (Numbers 21).
Moses gave Heshbon to the tribe of Reuben (Joshua 13).
Heshbon was assigned to the Levites (Joshua 21).
Isaiah lamented over Heshbon in his oracle against Moab (Isaiah 15).

negeb_885.name: Negeb
negeb_885.what: The dry southern region of Judah, stretching south from Hebron toward the Sinai.
key: Abram journeyed by stages toward the Negeb (Genesis 12).
Isaac was living in the Negeb when Rebekah arrived (Genesis 24).
Moses told the spies to go up into the Negeb and the hill country (Numbers 13).
Joshua struck the whole land, including the Negeb (Joshua 10).
David told Achish he had raided the Negeb of Judah (1 Samuel 27).

gibeon_470.name: Gibeon
gibeon_470.what: A Hivite city northwest of Jerusalem that made a treaty with Israel by deception.
gibeon_470.today: El-Jib, northwest of Jerusalem, West Bank
key: The Gibeonites tricked Joshua into making a peace treaty (Joshua 9).
The sun stood still while Joshua defended Gibeon against five kings (Joshua 10).
David's and Ish-bosheth's men fought beside the pool of Gibeon (2 Samuel 2).
God appeared to Solomon in a dream at Gibeon and offered him wisdom (1 Kings 3).
The tabernacle remained at the high place at Gibeon (1 Chronicles 16).

gilgal_476.name: Gilgal
gilgal_476.what: Israel's first camp west of the Jordan near Jericho, later a place of worship and assembly.
gilgal_476.today: Near Jericho, West Bank; exact site unknown
key: Joshua set up twelve stones from the Jordan at Gilgal (Joshua 4).
Israel was circumcised and kept the Passover at Gilgal, and the manna ceased (Joshua 5).
The people made Saul king before the LORD at Gilgal (1 Samuel 11).
Saul offered a burnt offering at Gilgal without waiting for Samuel (1 Samuel 13).
Samuel rebuked Saul at Gilgal for sparing Agag and the Amalekite spoil (1 Samuel 15).

beersheba_170.name: Beersheba
beersheba_170.what: A town in the Negeb at the southern edge of Israel, linked with the patriarchs.
key: Abraham made a covenant with Abimelech over a well at Beersheba (Genesis 21).
The LORD appeared to Isaac at Beersheba and renewed his promise (Genesis 26).
Jacob offered sacrifices at Beersheba on his way to Egypt (Genesis 46).
All Israel from Dan to Beersheba knew Samuel was a prophet (1 Samuel 3).
Elijah fled to Beersheba to escape Jezebel (1 Kings 19).

bethlehem_218.name: Bethlehem
bethlehem_218.what: A town in Judah south of Jerusalem, the hometown of David and birthplace of Jesus.
key: Rachel died and was buried on the way to Bethlehem (Genesis 35).
Naomi returned to Bethlehem with Ruth at the barley harvest (Ruth 1).
Samuel anointed David, Jesse's youngest son, in Bethlehem (1 Samuel 16).
Wise men came to Bethlehem to worship the newborn king (Matthew 2).
Angels announced Jesus' birth to shepherds near Bethlehem (Luke 2).

euphrates_421.name: Euphrates
euphrates_421.what: The great river of Mesopotamia, often named as the far boundary of the promised land.
euphrates_421.today: Euphrates River, through Turkey, Syria, and Iraq
key: The Euphrates is named as one of the four rivers of Eden (Genesis 2).
God promised Abram land from the river of Egypt to the Euphrates (Genesis 15).
Josiah was killed opposing Pharaoh Neco, who was marching to the Euphrates (2 Kings 23).
Jeremiah hid a linen loincloth by the Euphrates as a sign (Jeremiah 13).
The sixth bowl dries up the Euphrates for the kings from the east (Revelation 16).

gath_442.name: Gath
gath_442.what: One of the five main Philistine cities, hometown of Goliath.
key: The ark was moved to Gath, and the LORD struck the city with tumors (1 Samuel 5).
Goliath of Gath challenged the armies of Israel (1 Samuel 17).
David pretended to be insane before Achish king of Gath (1 Samuel 21).
David lived among the Philistines under Achish of Gath (1 Samuel 27).
David lamented Saul and Jonathan, saying not to tell it in Gath (2 Samuel 1).

ai_36.name: Ai
ai_36.what: A Canaanite town near Bethel, where Israel was defeated before capturing it.
ai_36.today: Possibly et-Tell or Khirbet el-Maqatir, near Bethel, West Bank
key: Abram pitched his tent between Bethel and Ai (Genesis 12).
Israel was routed at Ai because Achan had taken devoted things (Joshua 7).
Joshua captured and burned Ai using an ambush (Joshua 8).
Men of Bethel and Ai returned from exile with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2).

mizpah_811.name: Mizpah
mizpah_811.what: A town of Benjamin north of Jerusalem where Israel often assembled.
mizpah_811.today: Likely Tell en-Nasbeh, north of Jerusalem, West Bank
key: Israel gathered at Mizpah before going to war against Benjamin (Judges 20).
Samuel led Israel in repentance at Mizpah, and God routed the Philistines (1 Samuel 7).
Saul was chosen king by lot at Mizpah (1 Samuel 10).
King Asa built up Mizpah with stones taken from Ramah (2 Chronicles 16).
Gedaliah governed Judah from Mizpah until Ishmael murdered him (Jeremiah 41).

nile_895.name: Nile
nile_895.what: The great river of Egypt, the source of the country's life and farming.
key: Pharaoh dreamed of seven cows coming up out of the Nile (Genesis 41).
Pharaoh ordered every newborn Hebrew boy thrown into the Nile (Exodus 1).
Moses struck the Nile, and its water turned to blood (Exodus 7).
Frogs came up from the Nile and covered Egypt (Exodus 8).
God judged Pharaoh, who claimed to have made the Nile for himself (Ezekiel 29).

shiloh_1081.name: Shiloh
shiloh_1081.what: A town in Ephraim where the tabernacle stood during the time of the judges.
key: Israel set up the tent of meeting at Shiloh, and Joshua cast lots for the land (Joshua 18).
Hannah prayed for a son at the house of the LORD in Shiloh (1 Samuel 1).
The LORD called the boy Samuel at Shiloh (1 Samuel 3).
The ark was taken from Shiloh into battle and captured by the Philistines (1 Samuel 4).
Jeremiah warned Judah to remember what God did to Shiloh (Jeremiah 7).

sidon_1093.name: Sidon
sidon_1093.what: An ancient Phoenician port city north of Tyre on the Mediterranean coast.
key: Israel served the gods of Sidon and other nations (Judges 10).
Elijah was sent to a widow in Zarephath, a town belonging to Sidon (1 Kings 17).
Ezekiel prophesied judgment against Sidon (Ezekiel 28).
Jesus passed through Sidon on his way back to the Sea of Galilee (Mark 7).
On the voyage to Rome, Paul was allowed to visit friends at Sidon (Acts 27).

nazareth_878.name: Nazareth
nazareth_878.what: A small town in Galilee where Jesus was raised.
key: The angel Gabriel announced Jesus' birth to Mary in Nazareth (Luke 1).
Joseph settled the family in Nazareth after returning from Egypt (Matthew 2).
Jesus was rejected in the synagogue of his hometown, Nazareth (Luke 4).
Nathanael asked if anything good could come out of Nazareth (John 1).
Peter healed a lame man in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth (Acts 3).

red_sea_986.name: Red Sea
red_sea_986.what: The sea between Egypt and Arabia that God parted for Israel to escape Pharaoh.
red_sea_986.today: Red Sea, including the Gulfs of Suez and Aqaba; exact crossing site debated
key: God drove the locusts of the eighth plague into the Red Sea (Exodus 10).
Pharaoh's chariots and army were drowned in the Red Sea (Exodus 15).
Rahab told the spies that Jericho had heard how God dried up the Red Sea (Joshua 2).
Solomon built a fleet at Ezion-geber on the shore of the Red Sea (1 Kings 9).
By faith Israel crossed the Red Sea as on dry land (Hebrews 11).

persia_938.name: Persia
persia_938.what: The empire that conquered Babylon and allowed the Jewish exiles to return home.
key: Cyrus king of Persia decreed that the exiles could rebuild the temple (2 Chronicles 36).
Opponents hired counselors to frustrate the rebuilding through the reign of Cyrus of Persia (Ezra 4).
King Ahasuerus held a great feast for the officials of Persia and Media (Esther 1).
Daniel's vision of a ram represented the kings of Media and Persia (Daniel 8).
An angel told Daniel the prince of Persia had withstood him (Daniel 10).

seir_1042.name: Seir
seir_1042.what: The mountainous land south of the Dead Sea where Esau's descendants, the Edomites, lived.
seir_1042.today: Mountains of southern Jordan, east of the Arabah
key: Jacob sent messengers to his brother Esau in the land of Seir (Genesis 32).
After meeting Jacob, Esau returned to Seir (Genesis 33).
God gave Mount Seir to Esau and told Israel not to fight them (Deuteronomy 2).
Men of Mount Seir were destroyed when their allies turned on them (2 Chronicles 20).

gomorrah_489.name: Gomorrah
gomorrah_489.what: A city near Sodom destroyed by God with fire for its wickedness.
gomorrah_489.today: Exact site unknown; probably near the Dead Sea
key: The king of Gomorrah was defeated in the war of the kings (Genesis 14).
The LORD rained sulfur and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah (Genesis 19).
Isaiah compared the rulers of Judah to the rulers of Gomorrah (Isaiah 1).
Jude cites Sodom and Gomorrah as an example of eternal fire (Jude 1).

hamath_516.name: Hamath
hamath_516.what: A city-kingdom on the Orontes River in Syria, marking Israel's ideal northern border.
key: Toi king of Hamath sent his son to congratulate David on his victory (2 Samuel 8).
Jeroboam II restored Israel's border as far as Hamath (2 Kings 14).
People from Hamath were resettled in Samaria by the Assyrians (2 Kings 17).
Zedekiah's sons were killed before him at Riblah in the land of Hamath (2 Kings 25).

carmel_278.name: Carmel
carmel_278.what: A town in the hill country of Judah, south of Hebron, home of Nabal and Abigail.
carmel_278.today: Likely Khirbet el-Kirmil, south of Hebron, West Bank
key: Saul set up a monument for himself at Carmel (1 Samuel 15).
Nabal, a wealthy man of Carmel, refused David's request, and Abigail intervened (1 Samuel 25).
Abigail, widow of Nabal of Carmel, went with David to Hebron (2 Samuel 2).
Hezro of Carmel was one of David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23).

jezreel_643.name: Jezreel
jezreel_643.what: A town in Issachar overlooking the Jezreel Valley, a royal residence of King Ahab.
jezreel_643.today: Tel Jezreel, near Afula, northern Israel
key: Elijah ran ahead of Ahab's chariot to Jezreel (1 Kings 18).
Jezebel had Naboth killed so Ahab could take his vineyard in Jezreel (1 Kings 21).
Jehu killed King Joram, and Jezebel was thrown from a window in Jezreel (2 Kings 9).
Hosea named his son Jezreel as a sign of judgment on Jehu's house (Hosea 1).

lachish_711.name: Lachish
lachish_711.what: A major fortified city in the lowlands of Judah, southwest of Jerusalem.
key: Joshua captured Lachish after defeating its king and his allies (Joshua 10).
King Amaziah fled to Lachish and was killed there (2 Kings 14).
Hezekiah sent tribute to Sennacherib, who was at Lachish (2 Kings 18).
Lachish and Azekah were the last fortified cities of Judah left against Babylon (Jeremiah 34).

gad_1286.name: Gad
gad_1286.what: The tribal territory of Gad, east of the Jordan in the region of Gilead.
gad_1286.today: Western Jordan, east of the Jordan River
key: Gad and Reuben asked to settle east of the Jordan because of their livestock (Numbers 32).
Gad's fighting men crossed the Jordan to help conquer Canaan (Joshua 1).
Moses' allotment of land to the tribe of Gad is described (Joshua 13).
Hazael of Syria struck the land of Gad east of the Jordan (2 Kings 10).

macedonia_747.name: Macedonia
macedonia_747.what: The Roman province in northern Greece, including Philippi, Thessalonica, and Berea.
key: Paul saw a vision of a man of Macedonia pleading for help (Acts 16).
Paul passed through Macedonia encouraging the churches (Acts 20).
The churches of Macedonia gave generously despite deep poverty (2 Corinthians 8).
The Philippians supported Paul when he left Macedonia (Philippians 4).
The word of the Lord sounded forth from the Thessalonians in Macedonia (1 Thessalonians 1).

mount_zion_860.name: Mount Zion
mount_zion_860.what: The hill of Jerusalem where God dwelt in his temple, also a picture of the heavenly city.
key: God promised Hezekiah that a remnant would go out from Mount Zion (2 Kings 19).
Mount Zion is praised as the city of the great King (Psalms 48).
Those who trust in the LORD are like Mount Zion, which cannot be moved (Psalms 125).
Believers have come to Mount Zion, the heavenly Jerusalem (Hebrews 12).
John saw the Lamb standing on Mount Zion with the 144,000 (Revelation 14).

asher_1287.name: Asher
asher_1287.what: The tribal territory of Asher along the Mediterranean coast in northern Israel.
asher_1287.today: Coastal Galilee, northern Israel, into southern Lebanon
key: Moses blessed Asher with plenty and favor among his brothers (Deuteronomy 33).
Joshua assigned the coastal lands of the north to Asher (Joshua 19).
Asher failed to drive out the people of Acco and Sidon (Judges 1).
Asher stayed by the coast rather than join Deborah's battle (Judges 5).

dan_323.name: Dan
dan_323.what: A city at Israel's northern edge, formerly Laish, captured and renamed by the tribe of Dan.
key: Abram pursued the kings who captured Lot as far as Dan (Genesis 14).
The Danites captured Laish, renamed it Dan, and set up a carved image (Judges 18).
All Israel from Dan to Beersheba recognized Samuel as a prophet (1 Samuel 3).
Jeroboam placed a golden calf at Dan (1 Kings 12).
Ben-hadad of Syria conquered Dan at King Asa's request (1 Kings 15).

ekron_364.name: Ekron
ekron_364.what: The northernmost of the five main Philistine cities.
key: Ekron is listed among the five Philistine cities still unconquered (Joshua 13).
When the ark reached Ekron, its people cried out in panic (1 Samuel 5).
Israel chased the Philistines to Ekron after Goliath fell (1 Samuel 17).
King Ahaziah sent to inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron (2 Kings 1).

mount_sinai_855.name: Mount Sinai
mount_sinai_855.what: The mountain in the wilderness where God gave Israel his law and made his covenant with them.
mount_sinai_855.today: Traditionally Jebel Musa, southern Sinai Peninsula, Egypt; exact site debated
key: The LORD descended on Mount Sinai in fire as Israel trembled below (Exodus 19).
Moses stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights (Exodus 24).
God gave Moses the two tablets of the testimony on Mount Sinai (Exodus 31).
Moses came down with new tablets, his face shining (Exodus 34).
Paul compares Hagar to Mount Sinai, representing the old covenant (Galatians 4).

ramoth-gilead_984.name: Ramoth-gilead
ramoth-gilead_984.what: A fortified city in Gilead east of the Jordan, often contested between Israel and Syria.
key: Ramoth-gilead was the center of one of Solomon's administrative districts (1 Kings 4).
Ahab was killed by a random arrow fighting the Syrians at Ramoth-gilead (1 Kings 22).
King Joram was wounded fighting Hazael at Ramoth-gilead (2 Kings 8).
Elisha's servant anointed Jehu king of Israel at Ramoth-gilead (2 Kings 9).

susa_1118.name: Susa
susa_1118.what: A royal capital of the Persian Empire, with a fortified citadel.
key: Nehemiah was in the citadel of Susa when he heard of Jerusalem's ruin (Nehemiah 1).
King Ahasuerus reigned from Susa and held a great feast there (Esther 1).
Haman's decree to destroy the Jews was issued in Susa (Esther 3).
The Jews of Susa defended themselves against their enemies for two days (Esther 9).
Daniel saw a vision of a ram and a goat while in Susa (Daniel 8).

tarshish_1139.name: Tarshish
tarshish_1139.what: A distant trading port, probably in the western Mediterranean, known for its large seagoing ships.
tarshish_1139.today: Possibly Tartessus in southern Spain; exact site unknown
key: Solomon's fleet of Tarshish ships brought gold, silver, and ivory every three years (1 Kings 10).
Jehoshaphat's ships built to sail to Tarshish were wrecked (2 Chronicles 20).
The psalmist prays that the kings of Tarshish will bring tribute (Psalms 72).
Jonah boarded a ship bound for Tarshish to flee from the LORD (Jonah 1).

ashdod_101.name: Ashdod
ashdod_101.what: One of the five main Philistine cities, near the Mediterranean coast.
key: Some of the Anakim remained in Ashdod after Joshua's campaigns (Joshua 11).
The captured ark was placed in Dagon's temple in Ashdod, and Dagon fell (1 Samuel 5).
King Uzziah broke down the wall of Ashdod (2 Chronicles 26).
Isaiah walked barefoot as a sign when the Assyrians captured Ashdod (Isaiah 20).
Nehemiah rebuked Jews whose children spoke the language of Ashdod (Nehemiah 13).

gaza_446.name: Gaza
gaza_446.what: The southernmost of the five main Philistine cities, on the coastal road to Egypt.
key: Gaza marked the southwestern border of the Canaanites (Genesis 10).
Samson carried off the doors of Gaza's city gate (Judges 16).
Samson died in Gaza, pulling down the temple of Dagon (Judges 16).
Amos announced judgment on Gaza for selling captives to Edom (Amos 1).
Philip met an Ethiopian official on the road from Jerusalem to Gaza (Acts 8).

west-manasseh_1291.name: West Manasseh
west-manasseh_1291.what: The territory of the half-tribe of Manasseh west of the Jordan, north of Ephraim.
west-manasseh_1291.today: Northern West Bank and north-central Israel
key: Moses blessed Joseph's tribes, including the thousands of Manasseh (Deuteronomy 33).
Manasseh received land west of the Jordan, including for Zelophehad's daughters (Joshua 17).
Manasseh failed to drive out the Canaanites from Beth-shean and other towns (Judges 1).
Ezekiel's vision gives Manasseh a portion in the restored land (Ezekiel 48).

amalek_53.name: Amalek
amalek_53.what: The territory of the Amalekites, a nomadic people of the Negeb and Sinai who attacked Israel.
key: Israel defeated Amalek at Rephidim while Moses' hands were held up (Exodus 17).
Moses commanded Israel to blot out the memory of Amalek (Deuteronomy 25).
Saul defeated Amalek but spared King Agag and the best livestock (1 Samuel 15).
David dedicated to the LORD the spoil taken from Amalek (2 Samuel 8).

asia_108.name: Asia
asia_108.what: The Roman province in western Asia Minor, with Ephesus as its leading city.
key: People from Asia were in Jerusalem at Pentecost (Acts 2).
The Holy Spirit kept Paul from speaking the word in Asia at first (Acts 16).
During Paul's two years in Ephesus, all the residents of Asia heard the word (Acts 19).
Paul reminded the Ephesian elders how he had lived among them in Asia (Acts 20).
John wrote to the seven churches in Asia (Revelation 1).

nineveh_899.name: Nineveh
nineveh_899.what: The great capital of the Assyrian Empire on the Tigris River.
key: Nineveh was built in the land of Assyria (Genesis 10).
Sennacherib returned to Nineveh and was killed by his sons (2 Kings 19).
The people of Nineveh repented at Jonah's preaching, and God relented (Jonah 3).
Nahum announced the destruction of Nineveh, the bloody city (Nahum 3).
Jesus said the men of Nineveh will rise up at the judgment (Matthew 12).

sinai_1098.name: Sinai
sinai_1098.what: The wilderness around Mount Sinai, where Israel camped for about a year after the exodus.
key: Israel traveled through the wilderness of Sin, between Elim and Sinai (Exodus 16).
Israel arrived in the wilderness of Sinai and camped before the mountain (Exodus 19).
Moses counted the men of Israel in the wilderness of Sinai (Numbers 1).
Israel kept the Passover in the wilderness of Sinai (Numbers 9).
The cloud lifted, and Israel set out from the wilderness of Sinai (Numbers 10).

beth-shemesh_234.name: Beth-shemesh
beth-shemesh_234.what: A Levitical town on Judah's border with the Philistines, west of Jerusalem.
beth-shemesh_234.today: Tel Beth-Shemesh, west of Jerusalem, Israel
key: Beth-shemesh was given to the priests as a Levitical city (Joshua 21).
The ark returned on a cart to Beth-shemesh, where some men looked into it (1 Samuel 6).
Jehoash of Israel defeated and captured Amaziah of Judah at Beth-shemesh (2 Kings 14).
The Philistines captured Beth-shemesh during King Ahaz's reign (2 Chronicles 28).

ephesus_400.name: Ephesus
ephesus_400.what: A major port city in the Roman province of Asia where Paul ministered for over two years.
key: Paul left Priscilla and Aquila at Ephesus (Acts 18).
A riot broke out in Ephesus over the goddess Artemis (Acts 19).
Paul said farewell to the elders of the church at Ephesus (Acts 20).
Paul urged Timothy to remain at Ephesus and correct false teachers (1 Timothy 1).
Christ told the church in Ephesus it had abandoned its first love (Revelation 2).

ramah_972.name: Ramah
ramah_972.what: A town of Benjamin north of Jerusalem, near the border with the northern kingdom.
ramah_972.today: Er-Ram, north of Jerusalem, West Bank
key: Deborah judged Israel between Ramah and Bethel (Judges 4).
King Baasha of Israel fortified Ramah to block access to Judah (1 Kings 15).
Jeremiah described Rachel weeping for her children in Ramah (Jeremiah 31).
Jeremiah was released from his chains at Ramah after Jerusalem fell (Jeremiah 40).

sheba_1067.name: Sheba
sheba_1067.what: A wealthy kingdom in southern Arabia, known for gold, spices, and incense.
key: The queen of Sheba visited Solomon to test him with hard questions (1 Kings 10).
The psalmist prays that the kings of Sheba will bring gifts (Psalms 72).
Isaiah foresaw people from Sheba bringing gold and frankincense (Isaiah 60).
Merchants of Sheba traded spices, gems, and gold with Tyre (Ezekiel 27).

caesarea_266.name: Caesarea
caesarea_266.what: A Roman port city on the Mediterranean, the seat of the Roman governors of Judea.
caesarea_266.today: Caesarea, on the coast of Israel
key: Philip preached in all the towns until he came to Caesarea (Acts 8).
Peter preached to the centurion Cornelius in Caesarea, and Gentiles received the Spirit (Acts 10).
Herod Agrippa was struck down by an angel at Caesarea (Acts 12).
Paul stayed with Philip the evangelist in Caesarea (Acts 21).
Paul was held in Caesarea and appealed to Caesar before Festus (Acts 25).

capernaum_274.name: Capernaum
capernaum_274.what: A fishing town on the north shore of the Sea of Galilee, Jesus' base of ministry.
capernaum_274.today: Ruins on the north shore of the Sea of Galilee, Israel
key: Jesus left Nazareth and made his home in Capernaum (Matthew 4).
Jesus healed a centurion's servant at Capernaum (Matthew 8).
Jesus healed a paralyzed man lowered through a roof in Capernaum (Mark 2).
Jesus warned Capernaum for not repenting despite his mighty works (Matthew 11).
Jesus taught that he is the bread of life in the synagogue at Capernaum (John 6).

cush_312.name: Cush
cush_312.what: The land south of Egypt along the upper Nile.
key: Tirhakah king of Cush marched out against Sennacherib (2 Kings 19).
The psalmist says Cush will stretch out its hands to God (Psalms 68).
Isaiah walked barefoot as a sign against Egypt and Cush (Isaiah 20).
Zephaniah foresaw worshipers bringing offerings from beyond the rivers of Cush (Zephaniah 3).

horeb_576.name: Horeb
horeb_576.what: Another name for Mount Sinai, the mountain of God where the LORD made his covenant with Israel.
horeb_576.today: Traditionally Jebel Musa, southern Sinai Peninsula, Egypt; exact site debated
key: God spoke to Moses from a burning bush at Horeb (Exodus 3).
Moses struck the rock at Horeb, and water came out for the people (Exodus 17).
The LORD made his covenant with Israel at Horeb (Deuteronomy 5).
Elijah fled to Horeb and heard the LORD in a low whisper (1 Kings 19).
Malachi called Israel to remember the law given at Horeb (Malachi 4).

naphtali_1284.name: Naphtali
naphtali_1284.what: The tribal territory of Naphtali in Galilee, west and north of the Sea of Galilee.
key: Moses viewed all Naphtali from Mount Nebo before he died (Deuteronomy 34).
Kedesh in Naphtali was set apart as a city of refuge (Joshua 20).
Tiglath-pileser of Assyria captured Naphtali and carried its people away (2 Kings 15).
Jesus settled in Capernaum, fulfilling Isaiah's word about Naphtali (Matthew 4).

river_244.name: Beyond the River
river_244.what: The Persian province west of the Euphrates River, which included Judah.
river_244.today: Modern Syria, Lebanon, Israel, the Palestinian territories, and Jordan
key: Officials of the province Beyond the River wrote to Artaxerxes against Jerusalem (Ezra 4).
Tattenai, governor of the province Beyond the River, questioned the temple rebuilding (Ezra 5).
Darius ordered the province's treasury to pay for the temple work (Ezra 6).
Nehemiah carried the king's letters to the governors of the province Beyond the River (Nehemiah 2).

zebulun_1289.name: Zebulun
zebulun_1289.what: The tribal territory of Zebulun in lower Galilee, between the Sea of Galilee and the Mediterranean.
key: Jacob said Zebulun would dwell at the shore of the sea (Genesis 49).
Joshua assigned Zebulun its inheritance in Galilee (Joshua 19).
Isaiah foresaw honor coming to the land of Zebulun and Naphtali (Isaiah 9).
Jesus' ministry in Capernaum fulfilled Isaiah's word about Zebulun (Matthew 4).

anathoth_63.name: Anathoth
anathoth_63.what: A Levitical town in Benjamin just northeast of Jerusalem, the hometown of Jeremiah.
anathoth_63.today: Likely near Anata, northeast of Jerusalem, West Bank
key: Anathoth was given to the priests as a Levitical city (Joshua 21).
Solomon banished the priest Abiathar to his estate at Anathoth (1 Kings 2).
Jeremiah was from the priests of Anathoth (Jeremiah 1).
Men of Anathoth plotted to kill Jeremiah (Jeremiah 11).
Jeremiah bought a field at Anathoth as a sign of future restoration (Jeremiah 32).

arabah_79.name: Arabah
arabah_79.what: The deep rift valley running from the Sea of Galilee through the Dead Sea to the Gulf of Aqaba.
arabah_79.today: Jordan Rift Valley, Israel and Jordan
key: Moses spoke to Israel beyond the Jordan in the Arabah (Deuteronomy 1).
Israel traveled along the Arabah road away from Edom (Deuteronomy 2).
The Dead Sea is called the Sea of the Arabah (Deuteronomy 3).
King Zedekiah fled toward the Arabah when Jerusalem fell (Jeremiah 52).

ephraim-territory_1292.name: Ephraim
ephraim-territory_1292.what: The tribal territory of Ephraim in the central hill country of Canaan.
ephraim-territory_1292.today: Central West Bank, around Shiloh and Bethel
key: Moses blessed Joseph's tribes, including the ten thousands of Ephraim (Deuteronomy 33).
Ephraim received its inheritance but did not drive out the Canaanites in Gezer (Joshua 16).
Joshua told Ephraim and Manasseh to clear the forested hill country (Joshua 17).
Joshua received Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim (Joshua 19).

kadesh_661.name: Kadesh
kadesh_661.what: An oasis in the wilderness south of Canaan, where Israel camped for many years.
kadesh_661.today: Likely Ein el-Qudeirat, northeastern Sinai, Egypt
key: Abraham lived for a time between Kadesh and Shur (Genesis 20).
The twelve spies returned to Moses at Kadesh with their report (Numbers 13).
Miriam died at Kadesh, and Moses struck the rock for water (Numbers 20).
Israel remained at Kadesh many days after refusing to enter the land (Deuteronomy 1).

keilah_681.name: Keilah
keilah_681.what: A fortified town in the lowlands of Judah, northwest of Hebron.
keilah_681.today: Khirbet Qila, southwest of Bethlehem, West Bank
key: David rescued Keilah from the Philistines but fled when its people might betray him (1 Samuel 23).
Rulers of the district of Keilah helped repair Jerusalem's wall (Nehemiah 3).

kiriath-jearim_701.name: Kiriath-jearim
kiriath-jearim_701.what: A Gibeonite town west of Jerusalem where the ark of the covenant stayed for twenty years.
kiriath-jearim_701.today: Likely Tel Kiriath-jearim, near Abu Ghosh, west of Jerusalem
key: Kiriath-jearim was one of the Gibeonite cities that made peace with Israel (Joshua 9).
The ark was brought to the house of Abinadab in Kiriath-jearim (1 Samuel 7).
David brought the ark up from Kiriath-jearim (1 Chronicles 13).
The prophet Uriah of Kiriath-jearim was executed by King Jehoiakim (Jeremiah 26).

libnah_728.name: Libnah
libnah_728.what: A fortified town in the lowlands of Judah, southwest of Jerusalem.
libnah_728.today: Exact site uncertain; possibly Tel Burna, Israel
key: Joshua captured Libnah during his southern campaign (Joshua 10).
Libnah was given to the priests as a Levitical city (Joshua 21).
Libnah revolted against King Jehoram of Judah (2 Kings 8).
Sennacherib's army was fighting against Libnah when he sent threats to Hezekiah (2 Kings 19).

antioch_68.name: Antioch
antioch_68.what: A great city of Roman Syria where believers were first called Christians.
key: Nicolaus, a convert from Antioch, was chosen as one of the seven (Acts 6).
Disciples in Antioch were first called Christians (Acts 11).
The church at Antioch sent Barnabas and Saul on their first mission (Acts 13).
Paul and Barnabas brought the Jerusalem council's letter to Antioch (Acts 15).
Paul opposed Peter at Antioch for withdrawing from Gentile believers (Galatians 2).
